note: One entry per invocable leaf command. `--quiet`, `--color`, `--help` and the `--json` alias are omitted from every input_schema as noise; output is json when stdout is not a terminal; and a command with `writes: true` changes nothing until --apply (plus --yes off a terminal).

tools.name: cli-conformance
tools.summary: Check that every operator CLI is registered and on the shared harness.
tools.when:
Run this after adding a CLI, or when `npm run check:cli` fails. It answers two questions the
generated reference cannot: is anything claimed that does not exist, and is anything present
that was never declared.
tools.description:
npm run cli-conformance -- — Check that every operator CLI is registered and on the shared harness.

Run this after adding a CLI, or when `npm run check:cli` fails. It answers two questions the
generated reference cannot: is anything claimed that does not exist, and is anything present
that was never declared.

Reports MISSING (the manifest names a file that is gone), NOT_CONVERTED and
NO_ENTRYPOINT_GUARD (a tier A/B tool that is not on the harness) and UNTIERED (a CLI-shaped
file the manifest omits). The census currently walks scripts/ops only — see the 🛑 note in
lib/cli/census.ts before widening it.

Read-only. This command changes nothing.

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 130. For this command, 1 = at least one finding.

Examples:
  npm run check:cli
  npm run check:cli -- --tier a

tier.description: Only report findings for files in this tier

format.description: Output format (default: json off a terminal)

tools.name: cli-reference
tools.summary: Regenerate the committed CLI documentation from the tools' own declarations.
tools.when:
Run this after changing any tool's defineCommand() block — its summary, flags, examples or
subcommands. The generated files are committed, and `npm test` fails when they are stale, so
this is the fix for that failure. Never hand-edit the generated files.
tools.description:
npm run cli-reference -- — Regenerate the committed CLI documentation from the tools' own declarations.

Run this after changing any tool's defineCommand() block — its summary, flags, examples or
subcommands. The generated files are committed, and `npm test` fails when they are stale, so
this is the fix for that failure. Never hand-edit the generated files.

Writes <dir>/CLI_README.md (the full --help), docs/cli-reference.md (an index only) and
docs/cli-tools.json (the machine catalogue). Discovery is the registry in lib/cli/tiers.ts,
not a glob, and a file is statically checked for `export const cmd` / `defineCommand(` /
`import.meta.url` before it is imported — importing an unconverted tool would RUN it.

WRITES. Dry by default: without --apply nothing changes and the report says what would. Off a terminal --apply additionally requires --yes, or it refuses with exit 2.

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 130. For this command, 1 = generated files are stale (--check), or a listed tool could not be loaded.

Examples:
  npm run cli:reference
  npm run cli:reference -- --apply
  npm run cli:reference -- --check
